settings.value: Workflow management system to create reproducible and scalable data analyses

Snakemake is a workflow management system that aims to reduce the
  complexity of creating workflows by providing a fast and comfortable
  execution environment, together with a clean and modern specification
  language in python style. Snakemake workflows are essentially Python
  scripts extended by declarative code to define rules. Rules describe
  how to create output files from input files.

value.name: Run Tests for Linux (os= 'Linux')
value.run:
pixi run --environment ${{matrix.env}} test-all \
  --splits 10 \
  --group ${{ matrix.test_group }} \
  --splitting-algorithm=least_duration \
  --showlocals \
  --show-capture=all

cd tests/test_report
pixi run -e ${{ matrix.env }} snakemake \
  --use-conda \
  --cores 1 \
  --report report.zip

value.name: Detect container build input changes
value.run:
if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
  base_sha="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
  head_sha="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
else
  base_sha="${{ github.event.before }}"
  head_sha="${{ github.sha }}"
fi

if [ "$base_sha" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ]; then
  changed_files="$(git show --pretty='' --name-only "$head_sha")"
else
  changed_files="$(git diff --name-only "$base_sha" "$head_sha")"
fi

if echo "$changed_files" | grep -Eq '^(Dockerfile|pyproject\.toml)$'; then
  echo "build=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
else
  echo "build=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi

value.name: Skip container image build
value.run: echo "No changes to Dockerfile or pyproject.toml; skipping container image build."
